issue_description: Pump pressure is lower than expected and the pump is noisy, with low pressure at the pump inlet.
root_cause: Insufficient suction pressure causes cavitation: the liquid entering the impeller eye drops below its vapor pressure and forms bubbles that sap pump performance and, when they implode, cause noise and erosion damage. The piping may seem to have adequate pressure and still fall short, because pressure drops as the liquid accelerates into the impeller eye (net positive suction head available lower than required).
recommended_fix: 1) Compare the net positive suction head available (NPSHA) of the system with the value the pump requires (NPSHR). 2) Refer to the NPSH margin recommendations in ANSI/HI 9.6.1.
source_name: Hydraulic Institute - Why pump pressure is lower than expected

issue_description: New or restarted pump runs but gives no pressure, as if it has lost its prime.
root_cause: Air entrainment or lack of prime: the system is not arranged to flood the pump with liquid, or the intake is not submerged enough and an air vortex pulls air in.
recommended_fix: 1) Make sure the system floods the pump to prime it. 2) If it does not, prime the pump separately for startup and keep liquid in it for later starts. 3) Check that the liquid is deep enough over the intake.
source_name: Hydraulic Institute - Why pump pressure is lower than expected

issue_description: Newly installed three-phase pump is loud and gives only about half to two-thirds of the expected pressure with very low flow.
root_cause: The pump shaft is turning in the wrong direction, which is more common than expected on newly installed pumps.
recommended_fix: 1) Check which way the pump shaft is spinning. 2) On a typical three-phase motor pump, swapping two of the electrical leads reverses the rotation. 3) Verify the direction of rotation of every new or reinstalled pump motor before running the system.
source_name: Hydraulic Institute - Why pump pressure is lower than expected

issue_description: Pump pressure is lower than expected on a system that runs under vacuum or negative inlet pressure, with no visible leak.
root_cause: Poorly tightened bolts or a cut gasket on the suction side let air into the system; negative inlet pressure does not produce an outward leak, so it is hard to see.
recommended_fix: 1) Check the tightness of suction-side bolts. 2) Inspect the gaskets and replace a cut one. 3) Re-test the pressure.
source_name: Hydraulic Institute - Why pump pressure is lower than expected

issue_description: Pump motor draws more current than expected, runs hot or trips.
root_cause: The pump runs at more flow or head than designed, the liquid is denser or more viscous than assumed, or the pump is less efficient (internal wear, or higher losses in seals, packing or bearings, or mechanical contact).
recommended_fix: 1) Fit a flowmeter and pressure gauges at the pump and compare flow and head with the pump curve. 2) Confirm the liquid's specific gravity and viscosity. 3) Look for internal wear, tight seals or packing, bearing problems and mechanical contact.
source_name: Hydraulic Institute - Why pump power is higher than expected

issue_description: Pump gives low pressure right after a rebuild.
root_cause: The pump was assembled incorrectly: wrong clearances, or wear rings that are missing or fitted wrongly.
recommended_fix: 1) Have the rebuild checked by professionals who know the pump and its design. 2) Verify the clearances and the wear rings.
source_name: Hydraulic Institute - Why pump pressure is lower than expected

issue_description: Motor draws more than its rated current, trips protection, and its windings are evenly darkened.
root_cause: The motor is overloaded: the connected load exceeds its full-load current rating. Overloading is named as the number one cause of motor failure.
recommended_fix: 1) Measure the current at the motor and compare it with the nameplate rating. 2) If it is overloaded, increase the motor size or reduce the load.
source_name: Electrical Academia (educational blog) - Electric motor failure causes

issue_description: Three-phase motor runs hotter than rated and cannot deliver its full power although the load is normal.
root_cause: Voltage unbalance (unequal voltages at the motor terminals): one winding overheats and its insulation deteriorates.
recommended_fix: 1) Check the voltage unbalance regularly; more than 2% needs action. 2) Check the surrounding power system for excessive loads connected to one line. 3) If it cannot be corrected, reduce the load on the motor or use a larger motor.
source_name: Electrical Academia (educational blog) - Electric motor failure causes

issue_description: One phase of a three-phase motor is burnt and distorted after a fuse blew.
root_cause: Single-phasing: one phase was lost from a blown fuse, a mechanical failure in the switching equipment or lightning, and the motor kept running on two phases.
recommended_fix: 1) Use correctly sized dual-element fuses and heaters. 2) Where single-phasing cannot be tolerated, fit an electronic phase-loss monitor that drops out the starter.
source_name: Electrical Academia (educational blog) - Electric motor failure causes

issue_description: Motor in an enclosure or a dirty place keeps overheating although the load is normal.
root_cause: Airflow through the motor is restricted by dirt, dust, lint or oil, or the motor sits in an enclosed area where the heated air is recirculated.
recommended_fix: 1) Clean the motor and its air passages. 2) Stop oil from leaking seals or over-lubrication coating the motor. 3) Add vents at the top and bottom of an enclosed area.
source_name: Electrical Academia (educational blog) - Electric motor failure causes

issue_description: Belt-driven motor has overloaded bearings, or the belt slips.
root_cause: The belt tension is wrong: too loose and it slips, too tight and it overloads the motor bearings.
recommended_fix: 1) Check the belt deflection with a straight-edge across the sheaves or a tension tester. 2) Move the drive component to reduce or increase the deflection.
source_name: Electrical Academia (educational blog) - Electric motor failure causes

issue_description: Motor and the machine it drives wear out their bearings early.
root_cause: The motor shaft and the driven load are misaligned.
recommended_fix: 1) Check the alignment on new installations and at periodic inspections. 2) Correct misalignment with shims under the feet of the motor or driven equipment. 3) If it cannot be corrected, use a flexible coupler.
source_name: Electrical Academia (educational blog) - Electric motor failure causes

issue_description: Motor that sits idle for long periods is rusty and its insulation has lost resistance.
root_cause: Moist air is drawn in as the motor cools after it is switched off, which rusts metal parts and weakens the coil insulation.
recommended_fix: 1) Fit a heating element so the motor stays dry. 2) If that is not practical, set up a schedule of short runs for motors that are seldom used.
source_name: Electrical Academia (educational blog) - Electric motor failure causes

issue_description: Motor is switched on and off many times an hour and keeps overheating.
root_cause: Over-cycling: starting current is five to six times running current, and most motors are not designed for more than ten starts per hour.
recommended_fix: 1) Use a motor with a 1.25 or 1.35 service factor instead of 1.00 or 1.15. 2) Use a motor with a 50 C temperature rise instead of the standard 40 C. 3) Force extra air over the motor to cool it.
source_name: Electrical Academia (educational blog) - Electric motor failure causes

issue_description: Motor bearing runs hot or noisy after re-greasing, or was packed full of grease.
root_cause: Too much or too little grease: too much can pop the seals and overheat the bearing, too little lets it run dry.
recommended_fix: 1) Use the correct grease. 2) Use the correct amount for the motor. 3) Do not fill the bearing housing beyond its capacity.
source_name: Emerson - Electric motor problems and diagnostic techniques (brochure)

issue_description: Bearing of a motor that is stopped most of the time shows flaking and early failure (brinelling).
root_cause: Background vibration while the motor is not running pushes the lubricant film away, so the roller and raceway cold-weld and the surface flakes.
recommended_fix: 1) Isolate the motor from background vibration. 2) Switch regularly with a backup motor.
source_name: Emerson - Electric motor problems and diagnostic techniques (brochure)

issue_description: Motor insulation fails early and the motor runs hotter than its rating.
root_cause: Insulation temperature above the rated value shortens insulation life; each 10 degrees C of excess halves it.
recommended_fix: 1) Clean the motor regularly to prevent overheating. 2) Keep the temperature within the insulation class on the nameplate.
source_name: Emerson - Electric motor problems and diagnostic techniques (brochure)

issue_description: Paper jams inside the fuser and a sheet is wrapped around the fuser roller.
root_cause: Paper outside the printer's supported specification, mixed paper in one tray, too tall a stack, tray guides pressing too tightly, or sizes and types set wrongly in the menu.
recommended_fix: 1) Let the printer cool: the inside may be hot. 2) Open the fuser access door and gently pull the jammed paper out with both hands, removing all fragments. 3) Do not use sharp objects and do not touch the centre of the fuser. 4) Fan the paper, do not overfill the tray, set the guides and the paper settings correctly. 5) Print a test page; if jams continue contact Lexmark support or a service provider.
safety_note: The inside of the printer may be hot; let it cool before clearing the jam.
source_name: Lexmark Support - Paper jams in the fuser (C792)

issue_description: Printer shows a jam error and paper is stuck in the fuser behind the rear door.
root_cause: A sheet of paper is jammed in the fuser unit.
recommended_fix: 1) Wait at least 40 minutes for the fuser to cool down. 2) Open the rear door, raise both green levers to open the fuser and raise the green handle to open the paper guide. 3) Remove the jammed paper and return the levers and handle to their original positions.
safety_note: The fuser unit can be very hot and must be handled with care: wait at least 40 minutes for it to cool.
source_name: Xerox Support - Clear a paper jam from the fuser area (VersaLink B405)

issue_description: Colour laser prints show streaks, lines or spots.
root_cause: Contamination, dirt or debris in the paper path, such as on the printhead lenses or transfer belt, or old or damp paper or paper outside specification.
recommended_fix: 1) Clean the printhead lenses with the built-in cleaning tool. 2) Reseat the drum cartridges and the waste toner container. 3) Print the repeating-defects page to find the part at fault. 4) Replace the drum cartridge, or the fuser if the defect remains.
safety_note: The blade on the IBT cleaner is very sharp and the fuser may be very hot.
source_name: Xerox Support - Streaks, lines or spots on copies and prints

issue_description: Printer shows a paper jam message although no paper is visibly stuck.
root_cause: The printer is not feeding paper correctly, paper scraps are stuck in the print head path, paper is not loaded properly, the jam clear cover is not installed properly, or the PE actuator is missing or damaged.
recommended_fix: 1) Disconnect the machine from power. 2) Remove the jam clear cover and look for paper scraps or foreign objects and remove them. 3) Check the white PE actuator is in place; if it is missing, contact the maker's customer service. 4) Lift the scanner and check both ends of the platen for paper scraps, which may be soaked with ink and hard to see; move the print head gently by hand only with the power off. 5) Refit the jam clear cover so it is flush with the back.
safety_note: Disconnect the power before moving the print head and do not force it.
source_name: Brother Support - How do I clear the message PAPER JAM from the display?

issue_description: Paper jams and print quality gets worse after changing the paper.
root_cause: Paper that is curled, already printed on the other side, or not of a recommended type, or a media-type setting that does not match the paper.
recommended_fix: 1) Use the recommended paper. 2) Make sure the media type in the printer driver matches the paper in use. 3) Check the toner cartridge and drum unit are installed properly.
source_name: Brother Support - I'm having a problem with the print quality

issue_description: Colour laser prints have vertical rainbow-coloured or multi-colour streaks and 200.01 fuser jam errors.
root_cause: In most cases one or more damaged or defective imaging units (photoconductor units); a damaged or worn unit puts toner where it should not be and can also cause paper jams at the fuser.
recommended_fix: 1) Check that all four toner cartridges and imaging units are present and correctly installed. 2) Check the part numbers are supported by the printer. 3) Inspect each imaging unit for damage or wear and replace them one at a time until the streaks stop. 4) Contact Lexmark support if the problem remains.
source_name: Lexmark Support - 200.01 paper fuser jam and vertical rainbow lines (C925)

issue_description: Brother LED printer shows coloured vertical streaks down the page.
root_cause: The window of an LED head is clouded or dirty.
recommended_fix: 1) Compare the printout with the printed chart to find which colour's LED head causes the streaks. 2) Wipe that LED head window with a dry lint-free soft cloth.
source_name: Brother Support - I'm having a problem with the print quality

issue_description: Air conditioner is running but blowing warm air and not cooling the room.
root_cause: Dirty air filters, a refrigerant leak, wrong thermostat settings, electrical problems with the compressor, a failing blower motor or a failing compressor.
recommended_fix: 1) Replace clogged filters. 2) Set the thermostat to Cool and the fan to Auto. 3) Check the circuit breaker and the outdoor unit's power switch. 4) Clear plants from around the outdoor unit and clean the evaporator coil with a soft brush. 5) If that does not help call a professional HVAC technician: a refrigerant leak must be located, repaired and recharged by a technician.
safety_note: Turn the AC off right away if it blows warm air: running a malfunctioning system can overheat the compressor and damage it permanently.
source_name: Carrier - Why is my AC blowing hot air?

issue_description: Water is dripping from the indoor air handler and pooling on the floor.
root_cause: A disconnected or clogged drain tube or an old or damaged drain pan, dirty filters causing extra condensation, a frozen or dirty evaporator coil, a damaged condenser, or an installation problem.
recommended_fix: 1) Clean the drain pan and drain components and replace dirty filters: the page leaves only these two to the owner. 2) For anything else call a qualified professional, because attempting to fix the problem yourself can lead to injury and further damage. 3) If the unit was installed recently, call the installing contractor.
source_name: Lennox - Why is your air conditioner leaking water?

issue_description: Air conditioner never starts cooling although it is on, or blows warm air, with the thermostat showing the right room temperature.
root_cause: The thermostat is set wrongly (for example to Heat or Fan Only) or misreads the room temperature.
recommended_fix: 1) Set the thermostat to Cool and the fan to Auto, not On. 2) Replace the batteries or recalibrate the thermostat.
source_name: Carrier - Why is my AC blowing hot air?

issue_description: Outdoor AC unit is silent and will not start, the breaker having tripped or a fuse blown.
root_cause: A tripped breaker or blown fuse.
recommended_fix: 1) Reset the breaker at the electrical panel if you are comfortable doing so. 2) If it trips again straight away, get professional repair: there is an overloaded circuit or another electrical hazard.
safety_note: A breaker that trips again immediately points to an overloaded circuit or other electrical hazard that needs fast professional repair.
source_name: Lennox - Outside AC unit not turning on

issue_description: Outdoor AC unit buzzes or hums but its fan does not spin and it does not run.
root_cause: A failed capacitor: capacitors help start the compressor and keep the fan blades spinning, and can be damaged by high temperatures and power surges or wear out with age.
recommended_fix: 1) Have a professional HVAC technician replace the failed capacitor.
source_name: Lennox - Outside AC unit not turning on

issue_description: Ice has formed on the indoor coil and the AC does not turn on or does not cool.
root_cause: Airflow problems, most often a dirty or clogged air filter, or a refrigerant charge problem such as a leak.
recommended_fix: 1) Turn the system off and let the coil thaw completely. 2) Replace the filter (every three months). 3) Have a professional HVAC technician inspect the system for a blocked condensate line, a malfunctioning fan or a refrigerant leak.
safety_note: Do not handle refrigerant yourself: it can be dangerous and technicians need EPA certification.
source_name: Lennox - Outside AC unit not turning on

issue_description: AC shuts itself off and water collects in the evaporator drain pan.
root_cause: A tripped float switch: the water level in the drain pan rose too high, usually because of a clogged condensate drain line.
recommended_fix: 1) Make sure the float switch works and is not stuck. 2) Replace it if it is faulty. 3) Clean and inspect the condensate drain line and evaporator coil regularly.
source_name: Lennox - Outside AC unit not turning on

issue_description: AC runs but airflow from the vents is weak and the house does not cool.
root_cause: Dirty air filters block airflow and force the system to work harder; a failing or clogged blower motor also cannot move air effectively over the coils.
recommended_fix: 1) Replace clogged filters immediately (every 1 to 3 months). 2) Clear vegetation and obstructions around the outdoor condenser. 3) Clean the evaporator coil gently with a soft brush.
source_name: Carrier - Why is my AC blowing hot air?

issue_description: Outdoor condenser fan will not spin and the outside unit does not run.
root_cause: A worn-out fan motor (worn bearings or age), or debris such as sticks and leaves caught in the fan.
recommended_fix: 1) Clear debris from the outdoor unit. 2) Ask an expert to inspect the motor and say whether it can be repaired; if not, it may be time to replace the air conditioner.
source_name: Lennox - Outside AC unit not turning on

issue_description: Belt fasteners wear out early and cleaners get damaged, with carryback and mistracking.
root_cause: Unskived splices, or fasteners that interfere with the belt cleaners.
recommended_fix: 1) Skive the belt before applying splices where possible. 2) Use low-profile fasteners with a coined edge. 3) Follow the manufacturers' splicing instructions, including squaring the belt.
source_name: Flexco - Top 10 belt conveyor quick fixes (manufacturer blog)

issue_description: Belt rips right behind the splice or fails early.
root_cause: Fasteners that are too large for the smallest pulley.
recommended_fix: 1) Check the minimum pulley diameter (where the belt wraps 90 degrees or more) against both the belt maker's and the fastener maker's recommendations.
source_name: Flexco - Top 10 belt conveyor quick fixes (manufacturer blog)

issue_description: Belt slips on the drive pulley.
root_cause: Pulleys that are too small: the belt shrinks as it goes from full to partial tension and puts heavy pressure on the lagging.
recommended_fix: 1) Use the proper pulley diameter for the belt, as the engineers of the conveyor system recommend.
source_name: Flexco - Top 10 belt conveyor quick fixes (manufacturer blog)

issue_description: Belt wanders off to one side and its edge hits the structure.
root_cause: Mistracking: misaligned rollers or pulleys, an incorrect splice or material buildup.
recommended_fix: 1) Identify the cause of the mistracking. 2) Install a belt trainer. 3) Square the belt properly when splicing.
source_name: Flexco - Top 10 belt conveyor quick fixes (manufacturer blog)

issue_description: Material spills at the load zone and the belt is damaged there.
root_cause: Poor skirting and no impact protection.
recommended_fix: 1) Check and maintain the skirting with an easy-service system. 2) Add impact protection suited to the lumps.
source_name: Flexco - Top 10 belt conveyor quick fixes (manufacturer blog)

issue_description: Belt is cut or damaged by seized rollers.
root_cause: Seized, non-rotating rollers with sharp flat spots cut into the belt.
recommended_fix: 1) Inspect regularly for seized rollers. 2) Replace steel rollers, and composite rollers with a steel core, that have flat spots with sharp edges immediately. 3) Replace composite rollers without a steel core when feasible.
source_name: Flexco - Top 10 belt conveyor quick fixes (manufacturer blog)

issue_description: Without cargo the belt lifts out of the carrying idlers instead of settling into the troughs.
root_cause: Cupping: the belt exceeds its trough ability or is over-tensioned.
recommended_fix: 1) Check the belt without cargo: it should settle into the troughs. 2) Correct the tensioning, alignment and support.
source_name: Martin Engineering - 13 types of conveyor belt damage (manufacturer blog)

issue_description: Belt top cover shows narrow surface cracks.
root_cause: The belt is run over pulleys smaller than its minimum bend radius allows.
recommended_fix: 1) Keep to the belt's specified minimum bend radii. 2) Match the belt size to the pulley dimensions.
source_name: Martin Engineering - 13 types of conveyor belt damage (manufacturer blog)

issue_description: Belt plies separate and the edges swell in a wet or humid plant.
root_cause: A cut-edge belt's carcass absorbs moisture in a high-moisture environment and swells.
recommended_fix: 1) Switch to a molded-edge belt, which costs more but resists moisture.
source_name: Martin Engineering - 13 types of conveyor belt damage (manufacturer blog)

issue_description: Belt edge is worn or frayed because it keeps touching the surrounding structure.
root_cause: Edge damage: the belt mistracks and contacts the structure.
recommended_fix: 1) Monitor the belt alignment consistently. 2) Install tracking systems.
safety_note: Regulatory agencies may cite edge damage as a potential hazard.
source_name: Martin Engineering - 13 types of conveyor belt damage (manufacturer blog)

issue_description: Home standby generator shut down automatically with a LOW OIL PRESSURE alarm (error code 1300).
root_cause: Low oil level from oil consumption, oil leaks or lack of maintenance.
recommended_fix: 1) Let the generator cool for at least 30 minutes. 2) Check the oil level and refill; make sure the dipstick, oil fill cap, drain cap and oil filter are hand-tightened. 3) Look for visible oil leaks and fix them. 4) Clear the alarm and restart, never starting the generator under load. 5) If it keeps happening contact an authorized service dealer.
safety_note: Never start the generator while it is under load. Allow it to cool for at least 30 minutes before checking it.
source_name: Generac Support - Low oil pressure, error code 1300

issue_description: Portable generator will not start or runs roughly.
root_cause: Fuel shut-off off, empty tank, stale fuel or water in the fuel, dirty air filter, spark plug wire disconnected or bad plug, over-choking, low oil or a clogged carburetor.
recommended_fix: 1) Turn the fuel shut-off on and refill with fresh fuel (drain stale or watered fuel). 2) Clean or replace the air filter. 3) Reconnect the spark plug wire or replace the plug. 4) Set the choke correctly and fill the oil. 5) Clean the carburetor; for a rich mixture, lost compression or stuck valves contact the service dealer.
source_name: Generac Support - Portable generator troubleshooting quick reference guide

issue_description: Generator engine runs but there is no AC power at the outlets.
root_cause: The circuit breaker is open, a poor or defective cord, a bad connected device, a tripped GFCI outlet, or a fault in the generator.
recommended_fix: 1) Reset the circuit breaker. 2) Check and repair the cord set. 3) Try another device that is known to work. 4) Correct the ground fault and press the GFCI reset button. 5) Contact the authorized service dealer for a generator fault.
source_name: Generac Support - Portable generator troubleshooting quick reference guide

issue_description: Generator runs well with no load but bogs down when a load is connected.
root_cause: A short circuit in the connected load, an overloaded generator, a clogged carburetor or spark arrestor, or stale fuel; or engine speed too slow or a shorted generator circuit.
recommended_fix: 1) Disconnect a shorted load. 2) Reduce the load to the generator's limit. 3) Clean the carburetor and the spark arrestor screen. 4) Replace stale fuel. 5) Contact the service dealer for slow engine speed or a shorted circuit.
source_name: Generac Support - Portable generator troubleshooting quick reference guide

issue_description: Generator shuts down by itself, or starts and stops right away, and a light blinks on the side badge.
root_cause: Out of fuel or low oil, or the carbon monoxide protection shut it off (red light) or has a system fault (yellow light).
recommended_fix: 1) Refill fuel and the crankcase oil. 2) If the red light blinks, follow the safety instructions and move the generator to an open area outside, far from windows, doors and vents. 3) If the yellow light blinks and it keeps shutting off, contact the service dealer.
safety_note: A red carbon monoxide light means dangerous exhaust gas is accumulating: relocate the generator outdoors, far from windows, doors and vents.
source_name: Generac Support - Portable generator troubleshooting quick reference guide

issue_description: Generator engine surges or stumbles, or lacks power.
root_cause: The choke was opened too soon, a bad spark plug, a clogged carburetor or an overloaded generator or dirty air filter; carburetor mixture too rich or too lean.
recommended_fix: 1) Set the choke to the halfway position until the engine runs smoothly. 2) Replace a bad spark plug and clean the carburetor. 3) Reduce the load and clean or replace the air filter. 4) Contact the service dealer for carburetor mixture problems.
source_name: Generac Support - Portable generator troubleshooting quick reference guide

issue_description: Compressor will not start or stops during operation and the controller shows a motor overload problem.
root_cause: The motor overload relay, the fan motor overload or circuit breaker, or the motor thermistor has tripped, the phase sequence relay is open, or the wiring is interrupted.
recommended_fix: 1) Reset the overload once; if the problem keeps coming back, consult Atlas Copco. 2) If the phase sequence relay is open, check and correct the sequence of the connected phases at the machine's power inlet. 3) Interrupted wiring: consult Atlas Copco.
safety_note: Always isolate the compressor from its power supply and release all system pressure before opening any panels or inspecting internal components.
source_name: Atlas Copco - How to troubleshoot an air compressor

issue_description: Compressor air delivery or pressure is below normal.
root_cause: Air consumption exceeds the compressor's delivery, clogged air filters, air leaks, a malfunctioning solenoid valve, a clogged oil separator element, a leaking safety valve, or an inlet valve that does not fully open.
recommended_fix: 1) Check the air requirements of the connected equipment and add or replace compressor capacity if needed. 2) Replace clogged air filters. 3) Have leaks repaired and leaking tubes replaced. 4) Replace the solenoid valve or safety valve if faulty. 5) Replace the oil, oil filter and separator element if the separator is clogged. 6) Have the inlet valve inspected by Atlas Copco service.
source_name: Atlas Copco - How to troubleshoot an air compressor

issue_description: Compressor outlet temperature or delivery air temperature is above normal.
root_cause: Insufficient cooling air, low oil level, a dirty or clogged oil cooler, or on water-cooled units cooling water that is too hot, too little flow or a scaled or dirty circuit.
recommended_fix: 1) Check for cooling-air restriction, improve ventilation of the compressor room and avoid recirculation of cooling air. 2) Check the oil level and correct it. 3) Clean the oil cooler and keep the cooling air free of dirt; a clogged cooler needs Atlas Copco service. 4) On water-cooled units increase the water flow, check the temperature, and clean the water circuit and coolers.
source_name: Atlas Copco - How to troubleshoot an air compressor

issue_description: Safety valve blows after the compressor loads, or the compressor does not unload.
root_cause: The safety valve, the inlet valve, the minimum pressure valve or the solenoid valve is faulty, the oil separator element is clogged, or the dryer piping is blocked by ice.
recommended_fix: 1) Check the pressure setpoint and consult Atlas Copco service. 2) Replace a faulty solenoid valve. 3) Replace the oil, oil filter and oil separator element if the separator is clogged. 4) For ice in the dryer piping, inspect the refrigerant circuit and leaks and contact Atlas Copco.
source_name: Atlas Copco - How to troubleshoot an air compressor

issue_description: Condensate is not discharged from the condensate trap while the compressor is loaded.
root_cause: The discharge pipe of the condensate trap is clogged, or its float valve is malfunctioning.
recommended_fix: 1) Check the discharge pipe and correct it as needed. 2) Remove, clean and check the float valve assembly, and contact Atlas Copco if needed.
source_name: Atlas Copco - How to troubleshoot an air compressor

issue_description: Compressor starts running but does not load after its delay time.
root_cause: A faulty solenoid valve, an inlet valve stuck closed, a leak in the control air tubes, or a leaking minimum pressure valve.
recommended_fix: 1) Replace the solenoid valve if it is out of order. 2) Inspect and replace leaking control air tubes. 3) Have the inlet valve and the minimum pressure valve inspected by Atlas Copco service.
source_name: Atlas Copco - How to troubleshoot an air compressor

issue_description: Compressed air dryer reports a pressure dew point that is too high.
root_cause: Air inlet temperature or ambient temperature too high, inlet pressure too low, dryer capacity exceeded, a shortage of refrigerant, or a refrigerant compressor or condenser problem.
recommended_fix: 1) Reduce the air flow if the dryer's capacity is exceeded. 2) Correct high inlet or ambient temperature, using a pre-cooler or cooler air if needed. 3) Increase the inlet pressure if it is too low. 4) Have the refrigerant circuit checked for leaks and recharged by Atlas Copco.
source_name: Atlas Copco - How to troubleshoot an air compressor

issue_description: Water keeps showing up in the compressed air lines.
root_cause: Faulty air/oil separation, a failed or undersized dryer, a condensate drain that is not working, condensate lines that are not separated, wrong air treatment, temperature changes in the plant, or piping that traps water.
recommended_fix: 1) Check the air/oil separation system and change the separator element. 2) Inspect the condensate drains and drain lines and clean or replace defective parts. 3) Run piping sloped toward a receiver or drip leg with a no-loss demand drain. 4) Choose air treatment suited to the operating and ambient temperatures.
source_name: Kaeser - Industrial air compressor troubleshooting guide

issue_description: Oil is carried over into the compressed air lines.
root_cause: A worn or saturated oil separator element, or an overfilled oil sump.
recommended_fix: 1) Replace the oil separator cartridge and check the oil level and condition. 2) Drain the oil down to the correct operating level for the manufacturer's specification.
source_name: Kaeser - Industrial air compressor troubleshooting guide

issue_description: Air pressure at the tool or process is low although the compressor's own pressure is fine.
root_cause: The problem is in the distribution system: leaks, clogged filter elements, a fouled dryer heat exchanger, undersized piping or undersized air treatment.
recommended_fix: 1) Check lines, connections and valves for leaks. 2) Clean or replace the filter elements and clean the dryer heat exchanger. 3) Increase the pipe size after evaluation with a compressed air expert.
source_name: Kaeser - Industrial air compressor troubleshooting guide

issue_description: Compressor pressure is low at the compressor discharge and it cannot reach working pressure.
root_cause: The air capacity control is adjusted wrongly, valves are worn or broken, the air pressure switch is set wrongly, air leaks throughout the system, or the compressor is too small for the demand.
recommended_fix: 1) Adjust the capacity control and pressure switch as the manufacturer recommends. 2) Check the valves and repair or replace them as required. 3) Use an ultrasonic leak survey to find leaks. 4) Check that the compressor capacity meets total demand.
source_name: Kaeser - Industrial air compressor troubleshooting guide

issue_description: Compressor short-cycles (turns on and off frequently) and water shows up in the air, with worn or broken valves.
root_cause: Short cycling: the compressor does not run long enough to reach its operating temperature and burn off moisture, which also wears the valves. The cause can be an oversized unit or settings that do not fit demand.
recommended_fix: 1) Evaluate system demand, pressure settings and storage capacity. 2) Adjust the controls or add receiver capacity to keep proper run times. 3) Improve the duty cycle or downsize the compressor to match demand if it is oversized.
source_name: Kaeser - Industrial air compressor troubleshooting guide

issue_description: Compressed air system wastes energy and cannot build to working pressure because of leaks throughout the system.
root_cause: Air leaks throughout the system, which are among the most common and costly problems and the most often overlooked.
recommended_fix: 1) Inspect the whole compressor package for leaks. 2) Use an ultrasonic leak detection survey to identify and locate leak points.
source_name: Kaeser - Industrial air compressor troubleshooting guide

issue_description: Compressor makes unusual noise or vibrates, with knocking or rattling.
root_cause: Loose belts, pulleys or guards, worn or damaged bearings, or debris in the cylinder of a reciprocating compressor.
recommended_fix: 1) Inspect and re-tension or replace belts and secure all fasteners and guards. 2) For worn bearings contact factory-trained service. 3) On a reciprocating compressor stop immediately, inspect the cylinder and valves and contact service.
safety_note: Attempting internal repairs without proper training risks further damage and creates safety hazards.
source_name: Kaeser - Industrial air compressor troubleshooting guide

issue_description: Boiler turns on and off frequently (rapid cycling).
root_cause: A thermostat installed where drafts or heat affect it, a heat anticipator set wrongly, a wrong limit setting on a steam boiler, insufficient water flow through the boiler, or an expansion tank that is too small.
recommended_fix: 1) Move the thermostat to an inner wall away from heat sources and drafts. 2) Adjust the heat anticipator as the thermostat maker instructs. 3) On a steam boiler set the limit to the system's needs (maximum 220 F). 4) Check all valves to and from the boiler and confirm the circulator size. 5) Call a qualified service technician to check the expansion tank size and operation.
source_name: Weil-McLain - CGa, CGi, EG, PEG and LGB gas-fired boilers user manual

issue_description: Water keeps coming out of the relief valve of the boiler system.
root_cause: A flooded expansion tank, or an inoperative limit control on a steam boiler.
recommended_fix: 1) Call a qualified service technician to check the expansion tank operation. 2) On a steam boiler call a qualified service technician to replace the limit control.
source_name: Weil-McLain - CGa, CGi, EG, PEG and LGB gas-fired boilers user manual

issue_description: Boiler needs makeup water all the time and the water is black.
root_cause: Leaks in the boiler or piping, and oxygen corrosion from those leaks.
recommended_fix: 1) Have a qualified service technician repair the leaks at once, because constant makeup water brings in minerals that can cause boiler section failure. 2) Do not use petroleum-base stop-leak compounds. 3) Keep the pH of the water between 7.0 and 8.5.
source_name: Weil-McLain - CGa, CGi, EG, PEG and LGB gas-fired boilers user manual

issue_description: Popping or percolating noise comes from the boiler.
root_cause: Mineral deposits in the sections from constant use of makeup water, wrong boiler water pH, or insufficient water flow through the boiler.
recommended_fix: 1) Call a qualified service technician to de-lime the boiler if necessary. 2) Have leaks repaired so makeup water is not needed. 3) Have the pH checked and kept between 7.0 and 8.5. 4) Check all valves to and from the boiler and confirm the circulator size.
source_name: Weil-McLain - CGa, CGi, EG, PEG and LGB gas-fired boilers user manual

issue_description: Some radiators or baseboard units do not heat or are noisy.
root_cause: Air in the system, low system pressure, or on a steam boiler a high limit set too low.
recommended_fix: 1) Bleed air from the system through the air vents of the radiators or baseboard units. 2) Fill the system to the correct pressure and check for leaks; have a qualified technician repair them at once. 3) On a steam boiler adjust the high limit to a higher setting.
source_name: Weil-McLain - CGa, CGi, EG, PEG and LGB gas-fired boilers user manual

issue_description: Metal flakes are found at the vent outlet and the flueway is corroded.
root_cause: Contaminated combustion air, or condensation of combustion gases in the boiler sections.
recommended_fix: 1) Remove any contaminating products from the air supply and provide outside air for combustion. 2) Have a qualified service technician inspect the piping and controls to confirm the return water temperature is properly regulated.
source_name: Weil-McLain - CGa, CGi, EG, PEG and LGB gas-fired boilers user manual

issue_description: Boiler shuts down on a manual reset lockout because the air inlet or vent is blocked.
root_cause: The air inlet or vent is blocked; the boiler's control shuts it down automatically.
recommended_fix: 1) Remove easily accessible and removable blockages. 2) If the boiler shows a manual reset lockout, select Reset Lockout on the control display after removing the blockage. 3) If a blockage cannot be removed, have a qualified service technician check the boiler system.
source_name: Weil-McLain - CGa, CGi, EG, PEG and LGB gas-fired boilers user manual

issue_description: Boiler has no heat or has shut itself down on a safety fault.
root_cause: A dirty flame scanner, a faulty igniter or weak ignition transformer, an interrupted fuel supply, a low-water lockout, a failed burner motor, a faulty gas valve or a problem with the primary flame safeguard.
recommended_fix: 1) Check the manual fuel valves are open and the gas pressure is normal. 2) Check the sight glass for the correct water level. 3) Look at the flame scanner for dirt. 4) Call a qualified technician for any work on the ignition system, burner or controls.
safety_note: Do not bypass a safety device, troubleshoot internal control panel wiring, or repair the fuel train or pressure vessel yourself.
source_name: Cole Industrial (boiler service vendor blog) - Boiler troubleshooting

issue_description: Steam boiler runs but plant steam pressure and output are too low.
root_cause: Demand above the boiler's capacity, a failing feedwater pump or deaerator problem, steam leaks, steam traps stuck open, or scale on the heating surfaces.
recommended_fix: 1) Check whether new equipment or extra processes are overloading the boiler. 2) Check the feedwater pressure gauges. 3) Look for steam leaks and failed traps. 4) Have the boiler professionally cleaned if scale is suspected.
source_name: Cole Industrial (boiler service vendor blog) - Boiler troubleshooting

issue_description: Boiler fuel bill keeps rising and the flame looks lazy, yellow or smoky.
root_cause: An improper air-to-fuel ratio, faulty modulation, a dirty or fouled burner, scale on the tubes, or damaged insulation and steam leaks.
recommended_fix: 1) Have the burner tuned with a calibrated combustion analyzer. 2) Check for short cycling or constant high fire. 3) Look for soot on the fireside and for damaged insulation.
source_name: Cole Industrial (boiler service vendor blog) - Boiler troubleshooting

issue_description: Boiler locks out because the flame sensor cannot see the flame, or setpoints have drifted.
root_cause: A dirty or worn-out flame sensor, mechanical controls that have drifted from their setpoints, or a failed pressure or temperature control.
recommended_fix: 1) Verify the setpoints. 2) Check how the modulation motor responds to load changes. 3) Clean or replace the flame sensor. 4) If any safety device or operating control may be faulty, do not run the boiler.
safety_note: If you suspect any safety device or primary operating control is not working correctly, do not operate the boiler.
source_name: Cole Industrial (boiler service vendor blog) - Boiler troubleshooting

issue_description: Steam is made but does not reach the process, with water hammer or poor heating.
root_cause: A blocked steam pipe, steam traps stuck closed or open, condensate backing up, or foaming and priming from high dissolved solids.
recommended_fix: 1) Inspect the steam distribution system. 2) Test the traps. 3) Check the condensate return. 4) Review water chemistry and blowdown.
source_name: Cole Industrial (boiler service vendor blog) - Boiler troubleshooting

issue_description: Water leaks from the boiler pressure vessel, there is a smell of gas, a loud bang, or fire.
root_cause: Signs of a serious fault that the page treats as stop-and-call conditions: water leaking from the pressure vessel, a smell of gas, a loud banging noise or fire.
recommended_fix: 1) Carry out an emergency shutdown immediately. 2) Call for professional help. 3) Do not try to restart the boiler.
safety_note: Perform an emergency shutdown immediately and do not attempt to restart the boiler.
source_name: Cole Industrial (boiler service vendor blog) - Boiler troubleshooting

issue_description: Fridge runs but food is not cold enough.
root_cause: Too little clearance so heat cannot escape, blocked interior vents, too little food, wrong temperature setting, heat sources or sunlight, hot food, dirty or failing door seals, or frequent door opening.
recommended_fix: 1) Leave 2 inches of clearance at the back, top and sides. 2) Keep food 2 inches from the interior vents and keep the fridge at least two-thirds full. 3) Lower the temperature setting or use Power Cool. 4) Move it away from heat. 5) Let food cool before putting it in. 6) Clean the door seals and test them with a sheet of paper. 7) If food spoils early, request service.
source_name: Samsung Support - Cooling issues with refrigerator or freezer

issue_description: Refrigerator or freezer does not cool at all.
root_cause: No power, the unit left in Cooling Off (demo or shop) mode, or failing door seals.
recommended_fix: 1) Check the lights and panel to confirm there is power. 2) If the display shows OF OF or OFF OFF, turn off Cooling Off Mode. 3) Check the door seals with the paper test. 4) Unplug it or switch it off at the breaker for 2 minutes, then restore power and wait about three hours. 5) If it still does not cool, request service.
source_name: Samsung Support - Cooling issues with refrigerator or freezer

issue_description: Food freezes in the fridge compartment.
root_cause: Power Cool left on, food placed against the back wall or vents, vents blocked by ice or frost, or a room that is too hot or too cold.
recommended_fix: 1) Turn Power Cool off. 2) Keep food 2 inches away from the vents. 3) Clear ice from blocked vents. 4) Keep the room between 50 and 110 F. 5) If food still freezes, request service.
source_name: Samsung Support - Cooling issues with refrigerator or freezer

issue_description: Frost forms around the door and the fridge is warm inside; the door seal looks dirty or warped.
root_cause: Dirty or failing door seals let warm air in and the seal does not form a vacuum.
recommended_fix: 1) Clean the seals once a month with a damp cloth and dish soap. 2) Test them by closing a sheet of paper in the door: it should resist being pulled out. 3) If the seals are warped or damaged, request service.
source_name: Samsung Support - Cooling issues with refrigerator or freezer

issue_description: Samsung fridge is not cold and nothing seems to work: the plug or the outlet may be at fault.
root_cause: The plug is not fully inserted or the outlet or its circuit breaker has no power.
recommended_fix: 1) Push the plug in properly. 2) Plug another appliance into the same socket; if it does not work, try resetting the circuit breaker for that outlet.
source_name: Samsung Malaysia - 8 reasons why your Samsung refrigerator is not cooling

issue_description: New or newly reset refrigerator is still not cold a few hours later.
root_cause: It takes time: up to 4 hours for the display to show the set temperature and up to 28 hours to reach it if the doors stay shut.
recommended_fix: 1) Allow up to 28 hours without opening the doors before deciding there is a fault. 2) If the display is still blinking after 28 hours, request service.
source_name: Samsung Support - Cooling issues with refrigerator or freezer

issue_description: Haas CNC stops with servo error too large (alarms 103 to 106): an axis lags behind its command.
root_cause: A crash or hard stop, mechanical binding, lube starvation, or a failing motor or amplifier.
recommended_fix: 1) Read the alarm history to find the first alarm. 2) Jog the axis slowly through its full travel and watch the load meter. 3) Check the way lube before condemning any electronics.
safety_note: Lock out and tag out before opening the cabinet: servo drives hold a dangerous charge after power off.
source_name: Fabrico (maintenance-software vendor blog) - Haas CNC alarm codes troubleshooting

issue_description: Haas CNC shows servo overload (alarms 108 to 111): sustained excess current on an axis motor.
root_cause: Chip-packed way covers, a binding ballscrew, a dragging brake or overly heavy cuts.
recommended_fix: 1) Clean the ways and covers. 2) Jog the axes and compare the load meters across axes.
safety_note: Lock out and tag out before opening the cabinet; a vertical axis can drop when its brake is released.
source_name: Fabrico (maintenance-software vendor blog) - Haas CNC alarm codes troubleshooting

issue_description: Haas CNC shows an overvoltage alarm (119): incoming line voltage too high.
root_cause: The utility supply or the transformer tap setting.
recommended_fix: 1) Have a qualified electrician measure the incoming power and verify the transformer taps.
safety_note: Electrical measurements must be made by a qualified electrician.
source_name: Fabrico (maintenance-software vendor blog) - Haas CNC alarm codes troubleshooting

issue_description: Haas CNC shows low air pressure (alarm 120).
root_cause: Air pressure fell below the required threshold long enough to trip: compressor, regulator, clogged filter, leaks or an undersized drop line.
recommended_fix: 1) Watch the gauge at the machine while the machine cycles, not just at the compressor. 2) Look for leaks, a clogged filter or regulator and an air line too small for everything drawing on it.
source_name: Fabrico (maintenance-software vendor blog) - Haas CNC alarm codes troubleshooting

issue_description: Haas CNC shows low lube or low pressure (alarm 121).
root_cause: The way lube level or pressure is out of range: empty tank, clogged line, failed pump or metering unit.
recommended_fix: 1) Fill the tank. 2) Inspect the lines and metering points for flow.
source_name: Fabrico (maintenance-software vendor blog) - Haas CNC alarm codes troubleshooting

issue_description: Haas CNC shows regen overheat (alarm 122): the regen resistor overheated.
root_cause: High line voltage, or heavy acceleration and deceleration duty.
recommended_fix: 1) Check the line voltage first. 2) Then check the regen resistor and its wiring.
safety_note: Lock out and tag out before opening the cabinet.
source_name: Fabrico (maintenance-software vendor blog) - Haas CNC alarm codes troubleshooting

issue_description: Haas CNC shows motor overheat (alarms 135 to 138): an axis motor thermal trip.
root_cause: Sustained overload, binding or a high duty cycle.
recommended_fix: 1) Let the motor cool. 2) Find the mechanical cause of the load.
source_name: Fabrico (maintenance-software vendor blog) - Haas CNC alarm codes troubleshooting

issue_description: Haas CNC shows an encoder marker pulse fault (alarms 139 to 142).
root_cause: A contaminated or failing encoder, or a damaged cable or connector.
recommended_fix: 1) Inspect the encoder cable. 2) Look for coolant intrusion.
safety_note: Lock out and tag out before opening the cabinet.
source_name: Fabrico (maintenance-software vendor blog) - Haas CNC alarm codes troubleshooting

issue_description: Haas CNC shows communication failure with the motor control board (alarm 101) and random alarms.
root_cause: Noise, grounding issues or a genuine board failure.
recommended_fix: 1) Look at noise and grounding problems, the common triggers. 2) For a genuine board failure, call your Haas Factory Outlet (HFO) rather than swapping parts by trial and error; the page lists MOCON failures as worth an HFO visit.
source_name: Fabrico (maintenance-software vendor blog) - Haas CNC alarm codes troubleshooting

issue_description: Haas CNC shows emergency off (alarm 107): the E-stop circuit is open.
root_cause: The E-stop button is pressed, or the switch or its wiring is faulty.
recommended_fix: 1) Release the E-stop. 2) Inspect the button and the circuit.
source_name: Fabrico (maintenance-software vendor blog) - Haas CNC alarm codes troubleshooting

issue_description: Forks lift slowly or the load drifts down.
root_cause: Contaminated hydraulic fluid or low fluid, mast seal leaks or a cylinder failure.
recommended_fix: 1) Check the hydraulic fluid and the filters. 2) Inspect the mast seals and the cylinders for leaks. 3) Do not postpone small repairs: deferred repairs increase the risk of failure.
safety_note: Follow lockout/tagout when working on hydraulics, electrical systems or batteries.
source_name: Racklify (warehouse marketplace vendor blog) - Counterbalance forklift maintenance

issue_description: Forklift vibrates excessively when driving.
root_cause: The page does not name a single cause; it points to the tires, the wheel bearings and, on internal combustion trucks, the engine mounts as the places to check.
recommended_fix: 1) Inspect the tires. 2) Check the wheel bearings. 3) On IC trucks verify the engine mounts.
source_name: Racklify (warehouse marketplace vendor blog) - Counterbalance forklift maintenance

issue_description: Forklift brakes are weak.
root_cause: The page does not name a single cause; it points to the brake pads, the drums or discs and the condition of the hydraulic brake fluid as the places to check.
recommended_fix: 1) Inspect the brake pads. 2) Adjust the drums or discs. 3) Check the condition of the hydraulic brake fluid.
source_name: Racklify (warehouse marketplace vendor blog) - Counterbalance forklift maintenance

issue_description: Electric forklift battery does not hold its charge.
root_cause: Sulfation or improper charging.
recommended_fix: 1) Set up a battery care routine: watering, equalizing charges, correct charging cycles and battery change protocols. 2) Charge in a designated, ventilated area with PPE and spill kits.
safety_note: Follow lockout/tagout during battery replacement.
source_name: Racklify (warehouse marketplace vendor blog) - Counterbalance forklift maintenance

issue_description: Forklift brakes and brake parts wear out far too quickly.
root_cause: Operator practices: driving with the parking brake engaged, braking too hard, driving two-footed with the brakes partly applied, or damaging the wheel cylinder and hub seals.
recommended_fix: 1) Look for these driving errors in your facility. 2) Contact your Toyota dealer to arrange operator training. 3) Include the brakes in the pre-shift inspection, which OSHA and CCOHS require operators to complete.
source_name: Toyota Material Handling - Forklift safety and brake inspections

issue_description: UPS beeps twice every 15 to 45 seconds.
root_cause: The unit is running on battery power only.
recommended_fix: 1) Check that the unit is plugged correctly into the wall outlet. 2) Test the outlet by plugging the UPS into a different one. 3) If the other outlet works, have an electrician repair the faulty outlet.
source_name: CyberPower - Why does my CyberPower UPS product beep?

issue_description: UPS gives one long solid beep.
root_cause: The UPS is overloaded.
recommended_fix: 1) Unplug low-priority equipment and plug it into the surge-only outlets. 2) If that does not help, unplug the UPS from the wall after unplugging all equipment from it. 3) It may mean you need a larger unit.
source_name: CyberPower - Why does my CyberPower UPS product beep?

issue_description: UPS is beeping rapidly while running on battery.
root_cause: The battery is almost out of charge (about 25%).
recommended_fix: 1) Turn the UPS off because it is about to shut off anyway. 2) Note that the outlets will have no power once it is off.
source_name: CyberPower - Why does my CyberPower UPS product beep?

issue_description: UPS beeps three times every 30 seconds and the red fault LED is on.
root_cause: The battery failed the UPS's automatic test: weak capacity, a bad battery, or the battery is disconnected.
recommended_fix: 1) Let the UPS charge overnight, then run a battery test to confirm a weak or bad battery. 2) Reconnect or replace the battery. 3) The alarm repeats until the batteries pass a self test.
source_name: Vertiv - Liebert PST4 installer/user guide

issue_description: UPS runs in battery mode only, even though normal AC power is present.
root_cause: The input AC circuit breaker of the UPS has tripped.
recommended_fix: 1) Reset the circuit breaker by pressing the plunger back in. 2) If the breaker trips again after the UPS starts, reduce the load on the UPS.
source_name: Vertiv - Liebert PST4 installer/user guide

issue_description: UPS does not provide the expected runtime and the low battery LED lights.
root_cause: The batteries are weak or at the end of their useful life, or there are loose battery connections.
recommended_fix: 1) Charge the batteries for 8 hours and test again. 2) If the runtime is still short, the batteries may need replacing. 3) Check the battery connections.
source_name: Vertiv - Liebert PST4 installer/user guide

issue_description: UPS fault LED is on and the UPS sounds a constant alarm.
root_cause: The UPS detected an internal hardware fault.
recommended_fix: 1) In some cases the fault clears when the UPS is turned off and back on. 2) If the Fault LED stays on, call for a replacement unit.
source_name: Vertiv - Liebert PST4 installer/user guide

issue_description: UPS shows utility power but gives no output.
root_cause: The UPS is being controlled via its communications port by software.
recommended_fix: 1) Disconnect the computer cable from the UPS and press the On button. 2) If the UPS works normally, the software has control of it. 3) If it still has no output, call for service.
source_name: Vertiv - Liebert PST4 installer/user guide

issue_description: Screen stays black after boot but the power light is on, after a BIOS update, a battery or memory change, or an EC/RTC reset.
root_cause: The device has to run a full memory training on the next boot, during which it shows nothing for roughly 5 to 10 minutes (up to 10 minutes for 64 GB).
recommended_fix: 1) Connect the device to power. 2) Do not force a shutdown. 3) Wait patiently for memory training to finish and for the operating system to start.
source_name: ASUS Support - Device boot failure or no display after boot (black screen)

issue_description: Device will not boot into Windows after a BIOS update that was interrupted, for example by a forced shutdown.
root_cause: The BIOS update did not complete, so the system cannot start the operating system.
recommended_fix: 1) Keep the device connected to power. 2) If a failed-update screen shows, wait 60 seconds or choose Yes to start an automatic BIOS update. 3) If it asks for a file, download the BIOS for the exact model on another computer and copy it to the root of a FAT32 USB drive. 4) Switch the device off, hold the power button for 15 seconds, insert the USB drive and power on to complete the update. 5) For a black screen with the power light on, an EC or RTC reset is the suggested step.
source_name: ASUS Support - Device boot failure or no display after boot (black screen)

issue_description: Desktop has no display at startup after a discrete graphics card was installed or replaced.
root_cause: On desktops with Intel 13th generation CPUs and later, the system must first recognize the new card, and the monitor is plugged into the card's port.
recommended_fix: 1) Connect the monitor to the integrated graphics port on the motherboard first. 2) Start the computer. 3) In Device Manager look for Microsoft Basic Display Adapter, which shows the new card was recognized. 4) If the card does not appear, follow the graphics-card-not-detected guide.
source_name: ASUS Support - Device boot failure or no display after boot (black screen)

issue_description: Laptop sits at about 95% and does not charge to 100% while plugged in.
root_cause: This is the normal battery-protection (RSOC) behaviour of the device, not a battery or charging fault: charging does not resume until the level drops below 95%.
recommended_fix: 1) No repair is needed. 2) If you want it to reach 100%, unplug and reconnect the AC adapter a few times.
source_name: ASUS Support - Battery not supplying power or charging

issue_description: Laptop battery stops charging at 60% or 80%.
root_cause: Battery Care / Battery Health Charging in MyASUS is set to Balance mode (80%) or Maximum lifespan mode (60%).
recommended_fix: 1) Open MyASUS and check the battery care setting. 2) Choose Full capacity mode if you want the battery to charge to 100%.
source_name: ASUS Support - Battery not supplying power or charging

issue_description: Laptop battery is not charging or not supplying power.
root_cause: A mismatched, loose or damaged adapter or cable, a battery left uncharged for a long time, or a hardware state that needs a reset.
recommended_fix: 1) Use the original adapter and cable for that laptop and do not mix adapters between ASUS products. 2) Check the plug and jack for looseness and try another outlet. 3) Inspect the adapter and cables; if damaged visit a service center. 4) Connect to power and leave it charging overnight. 5) Try an EC reset, BIOS reset, the MyASUS battery diagnosis and, if needed, contact customer service.
source_name: ASUS Support - Battery not supplying power or charging

issue_description: Laptop or desktop overheats and the fan is loud, runs fast all the time, or does not run.
root_cause: A program using abnormal CPU or memory, dust buildup in the device or vents, poor surroundings (soft surfaces, blocked vents, wrong ambient temperature) or a fan worn down from long use.
recommended_fix: 1) Update BIOS, Windows and drivers and choose a suitable fan mode in MyASUS. 2) Check Task Manager for programs using too much CPU or memory. 3) Keep vents clear and use the device on a hard, flat surface at 5 to 35 C. 4) For dust, contact customer service, or clean from a distance with a compressed air can. 5) Run the MyASUS fan diagnosis and visit a service center if it reports a fault.
safety_note: When cleaning, turn off the device and disconnect the power cord. Do not blow it out with an air compressor, because excess pressure has damaged fan blades.
source_name: ASUS Support - Overheating and fan issues

issue_description: Fan does not spin when the computer is idle or under light load.
root_cause: By design, the fan stays off until the system temperature reaches a certain level, to save energy.
recommended_fix: 1) No repair is needed. 2) On some commercial desktops set MyASUS fan mode to Performance Mode, or on gaming desktops set Armoury Crate Fan Mode to Turbo, if you want the fan to keep spinning.
source_name: ASUS Support - Overheating and fan issues

issue_description: Surface tablet or laptop will not turn on, turns on and then off, or sticks on a black or logo screen.
root_cause: A connected accessory (USB drive, SD card, Type Cover, dock, external monitor) can stop it from turning on, or the battery is flat.
recommended_fix: 1) Disconnect all accessories and unplug it from the dock. 2) Connect the power supply made for the Surface and charge it at least 15 minutes. 3) Press the power button for about 20 seconds until the logo appears to force a restart. 4) If it still does not turn on at all, it needs to be sent to Microsoft for repair or replacement.
source_name: Microsoft Support - Surface won't turn on or start

issue_description: Switch port link light does not come on.
root_cause: No cable connected, wrong port, a device without power, the wrong cable type, a bad cable, loose connections, a faulty patch panel or media converter, a bad GBIC, or a port that is disabled.
recommended_fix: 1) Connect a known good device and check that both ends are in the right ports and both devices have power. 2) Swap the suspect cable with a known good one and reseat loose connectors. 3) Bypass patch panels and media converters. 4) Swap the GBIC. 5) Move the cable to a known good port and look for errdisable or shutdown status.
source_name: Cisco - Troubleshoot switch port and interface problems

issue_description: Link is up but slow, intermittent, or dropping, with rising CRC, FCS, alignment or runt errors on a full-duplex port.
root_cause: A duplex mismatch (one side full-duplex, the other half-duplex), a bad cable, a faulty switch port, or a NIC software or hardware problem.
recommended_fix: 1) Check the error counters on the interface. 2) Check the duplex setting on both ends of the link. 3) Replace a suspect cable and try another port. 4) Check the NIC on the connected device.
source_name: Cisco - Troubleshoot switch port and interface problems

issue_description: Switch port status shows errdisable and the port is shut down.
root_cause: The switch disabled the port after detecting an error such as an EtherChannel misconfiguration, a duplex mismatch, a BPDU guard and portfast conflict, or a UDLD one-way link.
recommended_fix: 1) Look at the interface status and logging to see why it was disabled. 2) Re-enable the port manually, or set an errdisable recovery timer. 3) Find and fix the root cause, because the port will go down again otherwise.
source_name: Cisco - Troubleshoot switch port and interface problems

issue_description: Gigabit link between two switches does not come up.
root_cause: The two ends use different GBIC types, or the cable is wrong for the GBIC or beyond its maximum distance.
recommended_fix: 1) Make sure both devices use the same GBIC type: SX with SX, LX with LX, and so on. 2) Check the cable type and length against the table for that GBIC.
source_name: Cisco - Troubleshoot switch port and interface problems

issue_description: Fiber link will not come up.
root_cause: Single-mode fiber on one port and multimode on the other, a cable that is wrong for the distance, or transmit and receive connected the wrong way round.
recommended_fix: 1) Use matching fiber types on both ports. 2) Connect the transmit lead of one port to the receive lead of the other port.
source_name: Cisco - Troubleshoot switch port and interface problems

issue_description: Link light is on but the port has many packet errors or keeps losing and regaining link.
root_cause: A marginally damaged cable or connector that is good enough to link at the physical layer but corrupts packets.
recommended_fix: 1) Check the cable on both sides of the connection. 2) Swap or replace the copper or fiber cable, and the GBIC if it is removable. 3) Rule out patch panels and media converters. 4) Try another port.
source_name: Cisco - Troubleshoot switch port and interface problems

issue_description: Connection problems between a Catalyst switch and a PC or third-party NIC (speed or duplex will not settle).
root_cause: Auto-negotiation issues between the switch port and the NIC, or old NIC firmware or driver.
recommended_fix: 1) Try hard-coding speed and duplex on both sides. 2) If neither auto-negotiation nor fixed settings work, update the NIC driver from the manufacturer's website.
source_name: Cisco - Troubleshoot switch port and interface problems

issue_description: Network performance collapses as if ports had problems, with the same frames repeating over and over.
root_cause: A spanning tree loop, which can happen when a port in a redundant topology stops receiving BPDUs and a blocked port starts forwarding.
recommended_fix: 1) Enable the STP loop guard feature, which puts a port that stops receiving BPDUs into a loop-inconsistent block state. 2) Check the design and the links for unidirectional failures.
source_name: Cisco - Troubleshoot switch port and interface problems

issue_description: Fiber link looks up but traffic only flows in one direction.
root_cause: A unidirectional link, caused by a broken fiber or other cabling or port issues, which the switch cannot detect on its own.
recommended_fix: 1) Repair the broken fiber or port. 2) Enable UDLD (aggressive mode on point-to-point switch links) so the port is put into errdisable when a one-way link is detected.
source_name: Cisco - Troubleshoot switch port and interface problems

issue_description: Home internet drops out; the router lights are off, flashing or red.
root_cause: The router has no power, or its connection has failed and needs a restart.
recommended_fix: 1) If the lights are off, check it is plugged in and powered on. 2) If they are flashing or red, unplug the power cable, wait 30 seconds to 1 minute, plug it back in and wait for the lights.
source_name: eSafety Commissioner (Australian government) - What to do when your home internet drops out

issue_description: Wi-Fi shows connected but there is no internet, or Wi-Fi is weak, while a cable works.
root_cause: A problem with the Wi-Fi signal, such as a router too far from the devices.
recommended_fix: 1) Disconnect and reconnect to Wi-Fi, then restart the router. 2) Connect a computer to the router with a cable. 3) If the internet works over the cable, move the router closer to the devices or add a Wi-Fi extender.
source_name: eSafety Commissioner (Australian government) - What to do when your home internet drops out

issue_description: Internet is down for the whole home and restarting the router did not help.
root_cause: Maintenance or technical issues outside the home, with the internet provider.
recommended_fix: 1) Check the provider's website or app for outages at your address. 2) If there is an outage the provider usually gives a restoration time. 3) If there is none, call or chat with the provider's support.
source_name: eSafety Commissioner (Australian government) - What to do when your home internet drops out

issue_description: Security camera picture is blurry or not clear.
root_cause: A dirty or cloudy lens, a cable run beyond the allowed range, a wireless camera too far from the router, or a varifocal camera that is out of focus.
recommended_fix: 1) Clean the lens with a soft, clean cloth. 2) Check the camera specifications for the allowed extension cable length, and keep a wireless camera closer to the router. 3) Adjust focus and zoom on a varifocal camera.
safety_note: Do not use harsh or aerosol cleaners on the lens, because they can harm it.
source_name: Reolink - Security camera picture problems and solutions (manufacturer blog)

issue_description: Security camera picture is washed out or too bright.
root_cause: The camera points directly at a bright light source such as the sun, a spotlight or a glass window, or the sunshade is not blocking enough light.
recommended_fix: 1) Do not point the camera straight at a light source or a glass window. 2) Slide an adjustable sunshade forward. 3) Adjust brightness and contrast.
source_name: Reolink - Security camera picture problems and solutions (manufacturer blog)

issue_description: CCTV picture has rolling horizontal or vertical lines moving across the screen.
root_cause: A ground loop problem of the power supply, or a faulty power supply.
recommended_fix: 1) Check the power supply of the camera (PoE or Wi-Fi camera) is working properly and replace it if it is faulty.
source_name: Reolink - Security camera picture problems and solutions (manufacturer blog)

issue_description: CCTV picture shows vertical lines that appear to shake in place.
root_cause: The camera and recorder or monitor use different video encoding standards, NTSC and PAL.
recommended_fix: 1) Check which standard your region uses and confirm that the camera and recorder both support it. 2) Most cameras can play both formats, so check the standard before buying.
source_name: Reolink - Security camera picture problems and solutions (manufacturer blog)

issue_description: CCTV picture glitches, flickers or freezes.
root_cause: Loose network connections, an unstable power supply, interference from nearby electronic devices, or software or firmware problems.
recommended_fix: 1) Check the physical cables and the power source. 2) Look for sources of interference. 3) Update the camera firmware.
source_name: Reolink - Security camera picture problems and solutions (manufacturer blog)

issue_description: Camera image is blurry at night.
root_cause: The camera has no infrared (IR) cut filter, so night vision is poor, and some indoor lighting can add to it.
recommended_fix: 1) Replace it with a camera with good night vision and an IR cut filter, especially for outdoor use.
source_name: Reolink - Security camera picture problems and solutions (manufacturer blog)

issue_description: Recorded or live video looks poor even though the camera is fine.
root_cause: The camera's resolution or stream setting is too low, for example a 480p or 720p camera or a high-megapixel camera set to a low stream, or a monitor that does not match.
recommended_fix: 1) Set the correct resolution on each camera, such as 2560x1440 or at least 1920x1080 on a 4-megapixel camera. 2) Use a monitor with a matching resolution.
source_name: Reolink - Security camera picture problems and solutions (manufacturer blog)

issue_description: Reverse osmosis water smells of rotten eggs but the untreated water does not.
root_cause: Bacterial growth on the membranes. If the whole house water smells of rotten eggs too, the membrane is not necessarily defective, because RO does not remove dissolved gases such as hydrogen sulfide.
recommended_fix: 1) Replace the membranes. 2) Compare with untreated water to see which case applies.
source_name: University of Nevada, Reno Extension - Installing and maintaining a reverse osmosis unit

issue_description: No trickling sound from the drain when the RO unit starts, and it does not work properly.
root_cause: The end of the wastewater line is in standing water or is blocked against the drain pipe, so waste water cannot flow freely.
recommended_fix: 1) Place the wastewater line so it can flow freely, with a large bend higher than where it enters the drain and an air gap in the P-trap. 2) Within fifteen minutes of turning the water on you should hear trickling from the drain pipe.
source_name: University of Nevada, Reno Extension - Installing and maintaining a reverse osmosis unit

issue_description: Reverse osmosis unit on a private well makes much less water than expected.
root_cause: Output depends on water pressure, and the well pressure-tank air pressure may be wrong.
recommended_fix: 1) Measure the air pressure in the pressure tank bladder with a tire gauge at the valve stem. 2) Set it as the manufacturer recommends. 3) If a community supply has too little pressure, use an RO system with a pump.
safety_note: Too much air pressure can rupture the bladder and ruin the tank, so follow the manufacturer's recommendation.
source_name: University of Nevada, Reno Extension - Installing and maintaining a reverse osmosis unit

issue_description: All water flow from the reverse osmosis unit stops.
root_cause: The sediment filter part of the unit may be clogged with sand or other particulates, or the membranes have reached the end of their life.
recommended_fix: 1) Replace the sediment filter, the cheapest part. 2) Replace the other filters at the same time. 3) Replace the membranes if they are worn out.
source_name: University of Nevada, Reno Extension - Installing and maintaining a reverse osmosis unit

issue_description: Chlorine taste returns in the treated water.
root_cause: The carbon filtration cartridge is overloaded.
recommended_fix: 1) Replace the carbon cartridge, which is much cheaper than the membranes.
source_name: University of Nevada, Reno Extension - Installing and maintaining a reverse osmosis unit

issue_description: Commercial reverse osmosis unit produces much less water in cold weather or on low inlet pressure.
root_cause: Cold feed water cuts production (water at 48 F cuts permeate output by 50%), and inlet pressure of 30 psi cuts it by more than half compared with 60 psi.
recommended_fix: 1) Raise the feed water temperature up to 80 F with a tempering valve. 2) Install a feed water booster pump to get 60 to 80 psi. 3) Check whether demand is above capacity and, if so, resize with a larger membrane or tank.
source_name: Pentair Everpure - EZ-RO systems installation and operation guide

issue_description: Commercial RO system is running out of treated water.
root_cause: A plugged prefilter, or a fouled membrane cartridge.
recommended_fix: 1) Change the prefilter. 2) Replace the membrane cartridge, every 12 to 24 months.
source_name: Pentair Everpure - EZ-RO systems installation and operation guide

issue_description: Commercial RO atmospheric tank repressurization pump is running but not pumping water.
root_cause: The pump is air locked.
recommended_fix: 1) Relieve the outlet pressure from the pump by draining the outlet so the pump can reprime.
source_name: Pentair Everpure - EZ-RO systems installation and operation guide

issue_description: Under-sink RO gives no water.
root_cause: The storage tank is under- or over-pressurized, the water supply is off or low (under 40 psi), a filter or membrane is clogged, the product line is crimped, or a ball valve on the tank is closed.
recommended_fix: 1) Set the tank pressure to 5 to 7 psi when empty. 2) Turn the supply on and check for at least 40 psi. 3) Replace clogged pre-filters or the membrane. 4) Remove any crimp in the line and open the tank ball valve.
source_name: ESP Water Products (RO retailer vendor blog) - Reverse osmosis troubleshooting guide

issue_description: Under-sink RO faucet flow is slow.
root_cause: A clogged pre- or post-filter, low air pressure in the RO tank, low water pressure, or a fouled membrane.
recommended_fix: 1) Replace the pre-filter and post-filter. 2) Raise the tank pressure to 5 to 7 psi. 3) Replace the RO membrane if it is fouled. 4) Allow 4 to 6 hours for the system to fill.
source_name: ESP Water Products (RO retailer vendor blog) - Reverse osmosis troubleshooting guide

issue_description: RO water has a bad taste or odor.
root_cause: A worn-out membrane, a system that needs sanitizing, an exhausted filter, or water that stood unused in the system.
recommended_fix: 1) Replace the membrane if TDS rejection is below 80%. 2) Clean and sanitize the system. 3) Replace the filter. 4) Use the system regularly and do not leave water standing in it more than 5 days.
source_name: ESP Water Products (RO retailer vendor blog) - Reverse osmosis troubleshooting guide

issue_description: RO system runs continuously.
root_cause: A faulty automatic shut off valve, low incoming water pressure (under 40 psi), low tank air pressure, a ruptured tank bladder, or a worn flow restrictor.
recommended_fix: 1) Replace the automatic shut off valve. 2) Raise the incoming water pressure. 3) Check the tank air pressure (5 to 7 psi when empty). 4) Replace the RO storage tank if the bladder is damaged.
source_name: ESP Water Products (RO retailer vendor blog) - Reverse osmosis troubleshooting guide

issue_description: RO ice or water is cloudy or milky.
root_cause: Tiny air bubbles from high oxygen content in the supply or from air in the lines of a new system or new filters, or a bad membrane.
recommended_fix: 1) Air bubbles go away with use. 2) If the problem remains, replace the RO membrane.
source_name: ESP Water Products (RO retailer vendor blog) - Reverse osmosis troubleshooting guide

issue_description: Washer spins slowly, stops mid-cycle or throws an error because of an unbalanced load.
root_cause: A small load collects on one side of the drum, or large items such as sheets and blankets tangle and weigh unevenly.
recommended_fix: 1) Add more items to a small load, or lower the spin speed. 2) Redistribute large items by hand and reduce the spin speed. 3) Match the cycle to the laundry.
source_name: Samsung Support - Washing machine spins poorly

issue_description: Washer shakes or vibrates excessively when it spins.
root_cause: The washer is not level and is not firm on all four corners.
recommended_fix: 1) Loosen the locking nuts (front load) and turn the legs: clockwise raises a corner, counterclockwise lowers it. 2) Keep the legs as short as you can. 3) Tighten the locking nuts and run a small load to check it does not shake.
source_name: Samsung Support - Washing machine spins poorly

issue_description: Front-load washer will not spin because it cannot drain.
root_cause: The pump filter is dirty. The washer drains before it spins, and if it cannot drain it never moves to the spin step.
recommended_fix: 1) Drain the water into a container through the drain hose. 2) Remove the pump filter by twisting it counter-clockwise. 3) Brush off dirt and check the impeller. 4) Refit the filter, close the drain hose cap and clean it about once a month or every 40 washes.
source_name: Samsung Support - Washing machine spins poorly

issue_description: Washer has drain and spin problems that build up over time, and the drain hose may be installed wrongly.
root_cause: A drain hose inserted more than 8 inches, or with an airtight seal, creates a siphoning effect; less than 6 inches and it can fall out.
recommended_fix: 1) Insert the hose 6 to 8 inches into the drain pipe and secure it with a zip tie. 2) Do not make an airtight connection. 3) Keep the hose between 18 and 96 inches high and check it for kinks. 4) If the hose is damaged, request service.
