source_name: Samsung Support - Washing machine spins poorly

issue_description: Washer drains by itself and shows an LC or 4C error code.
root_cause: The screw holding the drain hose to the back of the washer was removed.
recommended_fix: 1) Put the screw and holder back with any screw that fits. 2) If the holder is missing, service is required.
source_name: Samsung Support - Washing machine spins poorly

issue_description: LG washer shows an IE error and does not fill.
root_cause: The inlet hoses are clogged or twisted.
recommended_fix: 1) Look at the back of the washer for kinks, twists or curls in the hoses and straighten them. 2) Make sure the hose is firmly attached to its water supply.
source_name: Asurion (third-party repair guide) - Common LG washing machine problems

issue_description: LG washer shows an OE error and the tub is full of water.
root_cause: A clogged drain pump filter or hose.
recommended_fix: 1) Open the front panel, drain the water into a bowl through the drain pump hose, unscrew and clean the drain pump filter, and put it back. 2) If that does not help, press Spin Speed to High and listen for humming; no humming means the drain pump may need replacing by a professional.
source_name: Asurion (third-party repair guide) - Common LG washing machine problems

issue_description: LG washer shows an LE error and will not spin or agitate.
root_cause: The washer is overloaded, or it detects a foreign object such as a coin in the tub.
recommended_fix: 1) Remove some laundry and spread the rest evenly. 2) Check the tub for coins and other items and take them out.
source_name: Asurion (third-party repair guide) - Common LG washing machine problems

issue_description: LG washer shows a UE error.
root_cause: A very small load, or an unbalanced load.
recommended_fix: 1) Redistribute the laundry so it covers all sides of the drum. 2) Restart the cycle.
source_name: Asurion (third-party repair guide) - Common LG washing machine problems

issue_description: Washer thumps, shakes or walks across the floor during spin.
root_cause: The legs are unbalanced, so the washer is not level.
recommended_fix: 1) Put a level on top of the washer. 2) Adjust the legs with pliers or a wrench until they are even.
source_name: Asurion (third-party repair guide) - Common LG washing machine problems

issue_description: Water pools under the washer.
root_cause: A cracked or torn hose, a torn front door gasket on a front-load washer, or a detergent drawer that is not closed tightly.
recommended_fix: 1) Check the hoses for cracks and replace them if needed. 2) Look for tears in the door gasket; a professional can replace it. 3) Clean the detergent drawer in warm water and fit it properly.
source_name: Asurion (third-party repair guide) - Common LG washing machine problems

issue_description: Washer will not drain and there is no humming from the pump.
root_cause: The drain pump motor may be failing.
recommended_fix: 1) After cleaning the filter and checking the hoses, set the spin speed to High and listen. 2) If there is no hum, the washer may need a new drain pump, which requires a professional repair.
source_name: Asurion (third-party repair guide) - Common LG washing machine problems

issue_description: Elevator will not run properly or shuts down, and its doors do not work.
root_cause: Debris such as gum, wrappers, paper clips and coins in the car and hoistway door sills could stop the doors from operating properly, sometimes resulting in a shutdown.
recommended_fix: 1) Clean both sills. 2) If the car is stopped at a landing with the doors open, press the Door Close button until the doors close, then see if it returns to normal. 3) Check that every key switch is in the RUN position.
source_name: TK Elevator - EOX elevator owner's guide

issue_description: Elevator stopped working during a power failure or power fluctuation.
root_cause: Blown fuses or tripped circuit breakers in the mainline disconnect or meter room, or no full power from the power company.
recommended_fix: 1) Have your electrician check for blown fuses or tripped breakers in the mainline disconnect or meter room. 2) Confirm the building has full power from the utility. 3) After placing a trouble call, do not cycle the mainline disconnect, as that may clear diagnostic data.
safety_note: Have an electrician check the disconnect fuses.
source_name: TK Elevator - EOX elevator owner's guide

issue_description: Elevator is stalled with passengers inside.
root_cause: A stall or fault that leaves passengers trapped.
recommended_fix: 1) Immediately call the elevator service provider. 2) If a passenger is injured or ill, call 911. 3) Passengers can use the emergency phone in the car to speak to emergency response or dispatch personnel.
safety_note: Do not attempt to rescue the passengers yourself.
source_name: TK Elevator - EOX elevator owner's guide

issue_description: Lift stops between floors because of a power cut.
root_cause: Loss of normal power; without a standby power supply the elevators stop and stay at rest until power is restored.
recommended_fix: 1) With emergency power, the lift transfers to Emergency Power operation. 2) Some systems have auto-rescue, which moves the car to the next landing and opens the doors, or a battery lowering unit on hydraulic lifts. 3) Without standby power, wait for power to return and call the service provider if people are trapped.
source_name: TK Elevator - EOX elevator owner's guide

issue_description: Hydraulic elevator is slow or not at its best after standing unused for a long time.
root_cause: The oil in the power unit has cooled during the long rest.
recommended_fix: 1) Run the car up and down the hoistway for several minutes to heat the oil in the power unit.
source_name: TK Elevator - EOX elevator owner's guide

issue_description: Elevator suddenly shuts down and passengers are trapped.
root_cause: The elevator was loaded beyond its rated capacity, which causes a system fault and a shutdown.
recommended_fix: 1) Keep the load within the rated capacity. 2) Do not overload the car.
source_name: TK Elevator - EOX elevator owner's guide

issue_description: Elevator doors bind, drag or do not close completely.
root_cause: Doors that are out of alignment or adjustment, or that are not plumb.
recommended_fix: 1) Check the doors for ease of operation. 2) Have a properly trained elevator technician align or adjust them, because excessive looseness may cause a safety hazard.
safety_note: Excessive looseness of the doors may be a safety hazard and needs a trained elevator technician.
source_name: TK Elevator - EOX elevator owner's guide

issue_description: Elevator doors will not close or keep reopening.
root_cause: A blocked doorway: the infrared door edge detects an interruption of its beam.
recommended_fix: 1) Remove whatever is blocking the doorway. 2) The doors stay open until the blockage is removed.
source_name: TK Elevator - EOX elevator owner's guide

issue_description: Elevator stopped with its emergency signal sounding.
root_cause: The emergency stop switch was activated.
recommended_fix: 1) Return the stop switch to its normal position to restore normal operation.
source_name: Schindler - An owner's guide

issue_description: Elevator does not respond to calls at all.
root_cause: The power or MG switch in the locked service panel is turned off, and the elevator is not operable when it is off.
recommended_fix: 1) Authorized personnel should switch the power or MG switch back on, as it is normally left on for constant use.
safety_note: These switches are not for passenger use and should be used by authorized personnel only.
source_name: Schindler - An owner's guide

issue_description: Lift moves slowly or jerks.
root_cause: Poor lubrication, worn-out components, misaligned pulleys, or a motor or drive problem.
recommended_fix: 1) Lubricate the moving parts as the manufacturer's guidelines say. 2) If it persists, have it inspected and replace worn parts, realign the pulleys or repair the motor or drive.
safety_note: Make sure the lift is secure and isolated before troubleshooting.
source_name: Infraspeak (maintenance-software vendor blog) - 6 common lift issues

issue_description: Lift doors do not close or open properly.
root_cause: Misaligned door tracks, faulty door sensors, worn door rollers, or a door operator problem.
recommended_fix: 1) Check the tracks for obstructions or misalignment and clear or realign them. 2) Clean the door sensors. 3) If it persists, repair or replace the faulty parts or adjust the door operator.
safety_note: Make sure the lift is secure and isolated before troubleshooting.
source_name: Infraspeak (maintenance-software vendor blog) - 6 common lift issues

issue_description: Lift does not stop level with the floor.
root_cause: Leveling sensor problems, misaligned guide rails, worn suspension ropes, or uneven floor surfaces.
recommended_fix: 1) Check the leveling sensors for alignment and cleanliness. 2) Make sure the guide rails are free of obstructions and aligned. 3) If it persists, examine and adjust or replace the suspension ropes, and adjust the lift controller if needed.
safety_note: Make sure the lift is secure and isolated before troubleshooting.
source_name: Infraspeak (maintenance-software vendor blog) - 6 common lift issues

issue_description: Oil is found in the lift shaft, pit or control panel.
root_cause: Hydraulic or lubricating oil leaking from damaged seals, faulty valves or deteriorated hoses.
recommended_fix: 1) Find the source of the leak and repair or replace the damaged parts. 2) Clean the affected areas thoroughly. 3) Dispose of contaminated oil according to environmental rules.
source_name: Infraspeak (maintenance-software vendor blog) - 6 common lift issues

issue_description: Monitoring app shows the solar system offline or zero power.
root_cause: A Wi-Fi outage, router replacement, changed password, disconnected communication dongle or a platform interruption, while the inverter may still be generating.
recommended_fix: 1) Check the inverter's local display or status light. 2) If it shows normal operation, reconnect the communication device as the instructions say and confirm the router has internet.
source_name: SolaX Power - Solar system not working: troubleshooting

issue_description: Inverter stops generating or disconnects and shows a grid voltage, frequency or No Grid error.
root_cause: The grid voltage or frequency left its permitted range so the inverter stops exporting for safety, or there is a grid outage, a loose AC connection or a tripped protection device.
recommended_fix: 1) Confirm the property still has grid power and record the error. 2) It may reconnect by itself when grid conditions return. 3) If it keeps happening, especially around midday, ask an installer to inspect the AC wiring and grid conditions.
safety_note: Stop and contact a qualified installer if there is any sign of electrical damage or safety risk.
source_name: SolaX Power - Solar system not working: troubleshooting

issue_description: Inverter has no AC connection or is switched off after a breaker trips.
root_cause: An AC breaker tripped from an electrical fault, overload or water ingress, or an external isolator was switched off during maintenance.
recommended_fix: 1) Only check breakers and switches that are clearly labelled, safely reachable and covered by the installer's instructions. 2) If a breaker trips again at once, leave it off and contact a qualified installer.
safety_note: Do not repeatedly reset protective devices, because that can hide a serious fault.
source_name: SolaX Power - Solar system not working: troubleshooting

issue_description: Solar production drops during part of the day or on one string.
root_cause: New shade from trees, buildings, chimneys, antennas, leaves, bird nests or snow.
recommended_fix: 1) Check for new obstructions around the roof, from the ground. 2) Trim trees if they have grown. 3) For permanent shade ask the installer about microinverters or DC optimizers.
safety_note: Do not climb onto the roof to investigate.
source_name: SolaX Power - Solar system not working: troubleshooting

issue_description: Solar system shows zero output, the inverter shuts down repeatedly, or it displays a warning light or error code.
root_cause: The inverter entered protection mode because of an internal fault, abnormal grid conditions, excessive temperature, a DC input problem or a communication error; a blank display may mean it receives no power.
recommended_fix: 1) Check the inverter display, status light and monitoring platform. 2) Record the exact error code, inverter model and time of the fault. 3) Consult the user manual, and contact a qualified installer if zero production continues in full sunlight.
safety_note: Never open the inverter, disconnect DC cables or climb onto the roof to investigate a fault.
source_name: SolaX Power - Solar system not working: troubleshooting

issue_description: Off-grid solar battery is not charging, or the system shuts down early.
root_cause: Incorrect voltage settings, loose DC wiring, or a charge controller that has entered protection mode.
recommended_fix: 1) Check the LED indicators on the charge controller. 2) Make sure the battery voltage is not too low to wake the controller. 3) Verify the breaker between the controller and the battery is switched on.
source_name: SolaX Power - Solar system not working: troubleshooting

issue_description: Solar panel output is lower because of dust or bird droppings.
root_cause: Dust or bird droppings cause localized losses.
recommended_fix: 1) If safe and permitted by the installer's guidance, clean only from ground-accessible areas.
safety_note: Do not climb the roof to clean the panels.
source_name: SolaX Power - Solar system not working: troubleshooting

issue_description: Panels have cracked glass, burn marks, loose frames or hanging cables after a storm.
root_cause: Storm damage to the panels or wiring.
recommended_fix: 1) Do not touch it. 2) Stop troubleshooting and contact an installer to inspect.
safety_note: Do not touch damaged panels or cables; call an installer.
source_name: SolaX Power - Solar system not working: troubleshooting

issue_description: Centrifugal pump is noisy or vibrates excessively while running normally with the suction and discharge valves open.
root_cause: Coupling misalignment between the pump and its driver (the easiest to find and fix); a partially clogged impeller, which also shows as reduced head or flow; a broken or bent impeller or shaft; a foundation that is not rigid; worn bearings; suction or discharge piping that is not anchored properly; or cavitation.
recommended_fix: 1) Check the coupling alignment between the pump and the driver and correct it. 2) Remove any obstruction from the impeller. 3) Inspect for excessive run-out of the shaft and impeller; if either is broken or bent, replace it. 4) Check that the foundation is rigid and that the suction and discharge piping is supported correctly. 5) Check the bearings for wear. 6) If cavitation is suspected, review the net positive suction head available (NPSHA) of the system.
source_name: PSG Griswold (pump maker) Centrifugal Pump Minute, republished by Empowering Pumps (trade magazine) - Troubleshooting a noisy or vibrating pump

issue_description: Pump bearings run hot although the pump runs near its rated flow and head with the valves open.
root_cause: Misalignment between the pump and the motor, which causes vibration and extra load on the bearings; improper lubrication (wrong oil, wrong oil level, or oil that foams and so does not lubricate the bearings); or fluid hotter than 250 F, which heats the bearings and calls for a bearing cooler.
recommended_fix: 1) Check the alignment between the pump and its driver. 2) Make sure the oil sump holds the correct, non-foaming oil at the right level; most pumps have a sight glass for this. 3) For service above 250 F consider installing a bearing cooler, and make sure its cooling water lines are working properly.
source_name: PSG Griswold (pump maker) Centrifugal Pump Minute, republished by Empowering Pumps (trade magazine) - Troubleshooting: bearings run hot

issue_description: Pump leaks excessively at the shaft seal (packing or mechanical seal) although flow and head are normal.
root_cause: For a packed pump: the packing gland is not tightened properly, or the packing rings were installed with their slits lined up. For a mechanical seal: a score or nick on the shaft or shaft sleeve where the seal fits, or a worn or damaged seal (the seal flush system also affects how well a seal is maintained).
recommended_fix: 1) Packed pump: adjust the packing gland to reduce the leak (packing cannot be made to stop leaking completely, only controlled), then recheck the packing and make sure the rings are installed with their slits never aligned. 2) Mechanical seal: inspect the shaft or shaft sleeve under the seal for scores or nicks and replace it if damaged. 3) Replace a worn or damaged mechanical seal. 4) Look at the seal flush system and correct it so the seal is maintained properly.
source_name: PSG Griswold (pump maker) Centrifugal Pump Minute, republished by Empowering Pumps (trade magazine) - Troubleshooting: excessive seal leakage
